bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- End-to-end manufacturing capabilities supporting a diversified portfolio of products and services
- Three-segment structure spanning CDMO, complex hospital generics and consumer healthcare, serving both institutional and retail customers
- Global reach — markets served across PAN India and over 100 countries, with exports at 72.78% of turnover
- Board-level governance and control framework assessed as adequate and effective, with no qualification in the statutory, secretarial or cost audit reports
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Product quality and safety — Identified as a material risk in the BRSR: the Company's ability to meet patient needs, create value and build trust is directly linked to the quality and safety of its products, and poor performance in these critical areas can have negative impacts on stakeholders and in turn on the business. Mitigation is a shift from 'Quality for Compliance' to 'Quality as a Culture' across systems, processes, technology and people, with a dedicated Corporate Quality Assurance Group monitoring adherence to defined product quality standards.
- Business ethics — bribery, corruption and lobbying compliance — Identified as a material risk in the BRSR: PPL is subject to regulations related to bribery, corruption, lobbying and similar areas, and as standards keep changing any non-compliance may result in financial impact and harm to reputation. Mitigated through codes of conduct for board members, senior management, employees, suppliers, vendors and contractors across the value chain.
- Data privacy and data security — Identified as a material risk in the BRSR: a data breach within the Company's IT systems can lead to serious business impact and reputational risk, resulting in both financial and non-financial losses, with regulations tightening and awareness rising. Mitigated by a privacy policy governing personal information and by Vulnerability Assessment and Penetration Testing (VAPT) scans reported to IT and application teams.
- Patient, customer and consumer centricity under tightening regulation — Identified as a material risk in the BRSR: the Company must stay focused on the needs and wellbeing of patients, customers and consumers as regulations become stricter; addressed through its core principles of Knowledge, Action, Care and Impact and steps to improve engagement and outcomes, with patient centricity as a key priority.
- Export and geographic concentration — Structural concentration disclosed in the BRSR — exports contribute 72.78% of the entity's total turnover and markets served span over 100 countries, so earnings depend on overseas demand, regulatory regimes and currency movements rather than the domestic market.
- Single-activity concentration in pharmaceuticals — 100% of turnover comes from a single main activity — manufacturing of pharmaceuticals, medicinal, chemical and botanical products — leaving no diversification outside the pharmaceutical cycle.
- Employee attrition / talent retention — The permanent-employee turnover rate was 23% in FY2026 (25.50% in FY2025 and 21.94% in FY2024), against a much lower permanent-worker turnover of 5%, indicating sustained churn in the professional workforce that supports a science- and quality-led business.
- Market, credit and operational risks managed through the enterprise risk framework — The Board reports a Risk Management framework to identify, measure, manage and mitigate business risks and opportunities, which helps manage market, credit and operational risks and quantifies potential impact at Company level; details of the risk management process sit in the MD&A.

- Three-segment structure: CDMO (Piramal Pharma Solutions, an integrated contract development and manufacturing organization), Complex Hospital Generics (Piramal Critical Care) and Piramal Consumer Healthcare (over-the-counter consumer and wellness products).

outlook.body:
- Targeted investment in high-demand, differentiated CDMO capabilities — US$90 Million committed to the Lexington and Riverview sites for sterile injectables and payload linker capabilities
- Expansion of the CDMO commercial team to deepen customer engagement, alongside strengthened execution across network sites to ensure customer delight and secure repeat business
- Continued investment in differentiated and speciality products for the Complex Hospital Generics business, including the acquisition of the Kenalog brand from Bristol Myers Squibb and its integration into the existing portfolio
- Focused initiatives with suppliers to address supply constraints in the Injectable Pain Management portfolio
- Premiumisation of the Piramal Consumer Healthcare portfolio by launching fewer but higher-potential products with better success rates, with disciplined pricing and an improved channel mix
- Building out the e-commerce and digital channel in Consumer Healthcare while expanding offline reach in smaller towns and modern trade formats including super and hypermarkets
- Cost optimisation, operational excellence and prudent working capital management to protect EBITDA margins and cash flows
- Moving quality beyond regulatory compliance towards a culture of accountability and ownership, sustaining zero-OAI regulatory inspection outcomes
- Remaining aligned with the SBTi-approved decarbonisation roadmap, with heightened emphasis on increasing renewable energy adoption across sites
- BRSR reported on a consolidated basis with BRSR Core (Limited) assurance obtained from DNV Business Assurance India Pvt Ltd., with a Senior Vice President and Global Head - Sustainability & EHS designated as the BRSR reporting contact
- CSR obligations discharged in the education sector through the Aspirational Bharat Collaborative Program implemented by Piramal Foundation and the Piramal School of Leadership program implemented by Piramal Foundation for Education Leadership, both Section 8 companies; CSR policy anchored in the core values of Knowledge, Action, Care and Impact
- Gender diversity: women represent 30% of the Board of Directors and 50% of Key Management Personnel (standalone basis)
- Workforce disclosure: 6,617 permanent employees (21% female) and 6,774 total employees, with 3,666 total workers as at the end of FY2026
- POSH compliance with a gender-neutral policy covering employees, consultants, trainees, volunteers, third parties and visitors, and Internal Complaints Committee presence at corporate offices and site locations; 5 complaints received in FY2026, 2 resolved and closed and 3 under investigation, none pending beyond 90 days
- Compliance with the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961 including maternity benefits, leave entitlements and crèche facilities for eligible women employees
- Grievance redressal mechanisms in place for communities (dedicated human rights mailbox), investors, shareholders, employees and workers, customers and value chain partners under the NGRBC principles
- Codes of conduct extended beyond the Board and senior management to employees, suppliers, vendors and contractors as the ethical-practice framework across the value chain
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The principal expansion programme is a US$90 Million investment to scale sterile injectable and payload linker capabilities at the Lexington and Riverview sites; the Lexington expansion is scheduled for completion by the end of CY2027, while at Riverview already-commercialised enhancements are addressing growing demand for payload linker development and manufacturing. Capability build-out was accompanied by an expansion of the global CDMO commercial team and strengthened execution across network sites. At the plants, Mahad expanded Pharma Liquid production capacity by 4x and achieved a 25% capacity enhancement, improving throughput, asset utilisation and cost efficiency; two cartonators were added on the sachet line, along with a Vacuum Tray Dryer, an octagonal blender, a new inspection machine, upgraded water systems, a dedusting tunnel at raw-material receipt and additional HPLC capability in the QC laboratory. Turbhe invested in new equipment and developed scale-up processes to increase batch sizes of key products and commissioned a spray dryer facility (technology imported in FY2026) enabling innovative process development and larger final batch sizes. Pithampur replaced the conventional Multi Column Distillation Plant and Pure Steam Generator with a higher-capacity combo MCDP-cum-PSG unit, installed a 2500 KVA transformer with on-load tap changer, added Power Control Centre panels, containment and contamination-control systems, and an automatic bottle cartonator and laser printer on the bottle line. Dahej implemented a waste-stream recovery process for Sevoflurane manufacturing converting process waste into BAC-CP with commercial batch validation completed for large-scale production, plus an in-house Agitated Thin Film Evaporator recovery process for the BAC-AP project and a volute press for effluent sludge dewatering. Digwal Units 1 & 2 and PCC Unit 3 added a secondary vent condenser with cryogenic cooling, Kilo Lab data-logging integrated with a Rockwell DCS, continuous earth monitoring, VESDA fire detection and intrinsically-safe IO conversions that also enable easier future expansion. Ahmedabad (PDS and PPDS) upgraded research laboratories and imported analytical and formulation technologies including an LCMS-MS system, spray dryer and API-in-Capsule capability, all reported as fully absorbed.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- FY2026 was a transitional year: performance was impacted by inventory destocking by a key customer for a leading on-patent commercial product, soft early-stage CDMO order inflows in H1 on uneven US biopharma funding, and intensified competition in inhalation anesthesia across RoW markets
- Improving macro environment supported by stronger biopharma funding — up 75% YoY in H2 FY26 and 30% in FY2026 — plus a revival of strategic M&A activity in the US healthcare sector since September/October 2025
- Supply chain diversification and onshoring in the US is generating strong customer interest, expected to benefit the global network spanning India, the EU/UK and North America
- Recovery is most evident at overseas sites, where structurally stronger gross margins and higher utilisation can support improved EBITDA performance
- CHG expected to deliver stronger performance in FY2027, supported by ramp-up of inhalation anesthesia sales in markets outside the US and integration of Kenalog into the portfolio
- Growth in inhalation anesthesia outside the US progressed more gradually than anticipated owing to intensified competition; management expects a gradual pickup from FY2027
- Improved availability from initiatives to alleviate supply constraints in the injectable pain management portfolio is expected to support more consistent performance
- Consumer Healthcare positioned for consistent, profitable and faster-than-market growth on the strength of Power Brands, rising digital traction, an expanding distribution footprint and premiumisation
- Collectively these factors position the Company to deliver broad-based revenue growth accompanied by margin expansion in FY2027
- The RFP and order book pipeline began the financial year on a slow note but experienced a healthy rebound in the second half, supported by recovery in US biopharma funding and increased M&A activity in the US healthcare sector
- Since October 2025 the Company has recorded a significant increase in RFPs and a healthy pick-up in CDMO order inflows, particularly at overseas sites
- Renewed ecosystem confidence is translating into stronger pipeline momentum and enhanced visibility in the CDMO order book
- The development pipeline advanced with 157 molecules across various stages, of which 25 molecules are in Phase 3 and provide future opportunities as they progress towards commercialisation
- Differentiated service offerings contributed 40% of CDMO revenues in FY2026
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Piramal Pharma is a vertically integrated CDMO with growing specialty generics and consumer healthcare segments, benefiting from global supply chain diversification and high-margin contract manufacturing. Its strategic partnerships and capacity expansion position it for sustained revenue growth despite margin pressures in generics.

open.item: Management expects to deliver broad-based revenue growth accompanied by margin expansion in FY2027.
The Complex Hospital Generics business is expected to deliver stronger performance in FY2027, supported by ramp-up of inhalation anesthesia sales outside the US and integration of Kenalog.
Management expects a gradual pickup in inhalation anesthesia growth in markets outside the US from FY2027 after competition-driven softness.
Investing US$90 Million to scale sterile injectable and payload linker capabilities at the Lexington and Riverview sites, with the Lexington expansion scheduled for completion by the end of CY2027.
Focus on premiumisation of the Consumer Healthcare portfolio by launching fewer but high-potential products with better success rates and a clear emphasis on high-margin products.
Continue focused initiatives with suppliers and partner networks to alleviate supply constraints in the Injectable Pain Management portfolio and improve product availability.
Remain aligned with the SBTi-approved decarbonisation roadmap with heightened emphasis on increasing renewable energy adoption across sites.
Management flags intensified competition in inhalation anesthesia across markets outside the US as a drag on growth.

Management flags dependence on biopharma funding cycles and on a key customer, after inventory destocking by a key customer for a leading on-patent commercial product and soft early-stage CDMO order inflows in H1.
